units.title: Core content for all Art and Design titles

outcomes.text: Engage actively with the creative processes of art, craft and design in the chosen title and areas of study.
Grow as a reflective, enquiring and independent learner through art, craft and design.
Develop creative, imaginative and intuitive abilities when making images, artefacts and products.
Take creative risks, experimenting with ideas, processes, materials, techniques and digital or non-digital media.
Build critical understanding using personal interpretation, selected sources and independent judgement.
Refine ideas with an understanding of the context and influences behind them.
Know art, craft and design in historical and contemporary contexts, societies and cultures.
Understand the working practices and roles of the creative and cultural industries.
Understand the purpose, intentions and functions of art, craft and design and how they shape one's own work.
Acknowledge all sources in a bibliography and work safely.
Use a range of materials, techniques and approaches, digital, non-digital or both.
Use critical and contextual understanding to support practical work, and work to a brief or stimulus where suitable.
Use drawing for different needs and purposes without needing technical mastery.
Recognise that drawing includes mark-making, 2D and 3D designs, storyboarding, stitch and collage, in traditional or digital media.
Develop ideas through investigation by choosing and critically analysing sources.
Apply understanding of practices in the creative and cultural industries to own work.
Refine ideas by experimenting with media, materials, techniques and processes as work goes on.
Record ideas, observations and judgements visually and in annotation using specialist vocabulary.
Use visual language critically through safe and effective use of media, materials, techniques, processes and technologies.
Use drawing skills suited to the context.
Realise personal intentions through a sustained creative process.
Know the work and approaches of artists, craftspeople or designers from different periods, societies and cultures.
Know the historical and contemporary environments, situations or issues that shape work.
Use other sources researched in the chosen title and area of study.
Communicate meaning and intention through colour, line, form, tone and texture.
Know the properties and effects of different media, materials, techniques and processes and how they serve own intentions.
Understand the different purposes, intentions and functions of art, craft and design in various contexts.

units.title: Art, Craft and Design: Combined Titles (J170)

outcomes.text: Describe the course as broad-based, learning through varied processes, tools, techniques and materials.
Develop skills using traditional or digital techniques specific to two or more chosen titles.
Show greater breadth of approach, matched in demand to the single titles.
Explore critical and contextual sources, including historical and contemporary practitioners and the purposes of art, craft and design.
Work in two or more of Fine Art, Graphic Communication, Photography, Textile Design, Three-Dimensional Design and Critical and Contextual Studies.
Choose one area for two or more titles, such as still life in fine art and photography.
Alternatively combine different areas, such as typography and product design, in a complementary way.
Explore techniques suited to the areas of study within each chosen title.
Develop ideas through investigation of critically analysed sources.
Apply understanding of creative and cultural industry practices, refining ideas by recording, researching, selecting, editing and presenting.
Record ideas and judgements appropriately, for example by drawing and creating images in mixed media.
Use specialist vocabulary visually or in writing.
Use media, materials, techniques, processes and technologies safely and critically.
Use drawing for varied needs and realise intentions through a sustained process.
Understand how sources inspire the development of ideas.
Refer to practitioners, environments, situations and issues from contemporary and historical contexts.
Communicate meaning through colour, line, form, tone and texture.
Know how the properties of media, materials, techniques and processes suit own intentions.
Understand the varied purposes, intentions and functions of art, craft and design.
Define fine art as work made mainly for aesthetic, intellectual or conceptual purposes rather than practical function.

Explore the work of historical and contemporary fine artists and the purposes of fine art.
Show knowledge and skills within the chosen fine art areas of study.
Work in one or more of drawing, installation, lens- or light-based media and mixed-media.
Work in one or more of land art, printing, painting and sculpture, or combine areas.
Work creatively with painting and drawing in various media.
Use printing methods: screen printing, etching, aquatint, lithography and block printing.
Use stencils, carving, modelling, constructing, mosaic and mobiles.
Use environmental art, graffito, kinetic, light-based, digital and mixed media.
Develop ideas through investigation of critically analysed sources.
Apply understanding of fine art practice in the creative industries and refine ideas by recording, selecting, editing and presenting.
Record ideas and observations through drawing or photographing.

Work in one or more of typography, communication graphics, design for print and advertising.
Work in one or more of multi-media, illustration, interactive design (web, app, game), package design and signage.
Work with computer-aided design, web design, apps and games.
Work with letterforms and typography.
Work with drawing, book illustration, print, photography and package design.
Develop ideas through investigation of critically analysed sources.
Apply industry practice using image and typography, refining by researching, selecting, editing and presenting.

Work in one or more of documentary photography, photo-journalism, studio and location photography.
Work in one or more of experimental imagery, installation and moving image, or combine areas.
Make photograms and pinhole cameras and use chemical film processes.

subtopics.title: What critical and contextual studies is

outcomes.text: Define the title as critical analysis, interpretation and reflective appraisal of the work of artists, craftspeople and designers.
Develop skills through research and analysis in a critical and contextual setting.
Explore sources in written or practical form, or both, including historical and contemporary practitioners.
Analyse and interpret work in its historical, cultural, social, economic or political context to understand meanings, purposes, relationships and influences.
Work in one or more of artists, craftspeople and designers, genres, movements and themes, concepts and ideas.
Work in one or more of contemporary art, popular culture, the human form and still life.
Work in one or more of designed objects, landscape and natural forms.
Analyse and interpret the work of practitioners in its context.
Choose suitable methods and media to communicate responses and show understanding.

Record ideas by selecting and interpreting research and analysing materials and techniques of practitioners.
